The model is pretrained from scratch on physically motivated synthetic spectra in a self-supervised reconstruction task, and is then fine-tuned on observational LAMOST spectra to predict stellar parameters, with emphasis on metallicity ([Fe/H]). Experiments show that the model reconstructs low-SNR spectra with high fidelity and improves parameter estimation under noisy conditions. In the tested low-SNR setting, it achieves a metallicity prediction error of approximately 0.38 dex; even at extremely low-SNR values of about 1–2, it still provides useful information from spectra that are otherwise difficult to exploit.

title: High-resolution prediction and risk mapping of Haemaphysalis longicornis habitat suitability in the Jiaodong Peninsula, China
abstract: Ticks are vectors of numerous human pathogens, and accurate predictions of their spatial distribution are essential for the effective prevention and control of tick-borne diseases. High-resolution predictions remain scarce in China. To address this gap, a tick survey was conducted across the Jiaodong Peninsula at 2,647 points during the summer of 2024, integrating high-resolution environmental variables. Seven machine-learning algorithms were used, and ensemble learning was applied, resulting in a habitat-suitability map for Haemaphysalis longicornis at a 10-meter resolution. The ensemble model showed robust predictive accuracy (AUC = 0.8355). Summer normalized difference vegetation index was the primary environmental driver, followed by land use and land cover and winter normalized difference vegetation index. High risk villages accounted for 70.0%, 40.2%, and 16.9% of rural, urban rural fringe, and urban areas, respectively. Ensemble machine-learning provides a robust approach, revealing how ecological factors and human activities shape distribution patterns and risk heterogeneity.

title: Surface energy-directed assembly of liquid metal particles for intelligent wearable electronics
abstract: Liquid metals (LMs) are promising for flexible electronics owing to their high electrical conductivity and inherent room temperature deformability. However, their high surface tension poses major technical barriers for high-resolution patterning. While conventional pre-patterned metal seeding layers can enable deterministic LM patterning, this approach inevitably adds redundant fabrication steps and increases process complexity. Here, we develop a seeding-layer-free surface energy-directed assembly process based on ultrasonically dispersed, sodium alginate-stabilized LM particle dispersions, which enables high-precision LM patterning on various stretchable substrates. The fabricated strain sensors exhibit <200 ms response and >1,000-cycle stability, while the LM electrode arrays paired with a convolutional neural network achieve 94% accuracy in gesture recognition. This work establishes a high-precision, environmentally benign, and broadly applicable platform for next-generation LM-based flexible and stretchable electronics.

title: Long-term ambient benzene exposure increases incident NAFLD risk through accelerated biological aging
abstract: The contribution of ambient air pollutants to non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) remains undefined. This study included 401,472 adults from the UK Biobank (UKB), with residential benzene estimated at 1-km resolution from the DEFRA model (2006–2020). After multivariable adjustment in the Cox models, each interquartile-range (0.151 μg/m 3 ) increment in benzene was associated with a 26% higher risk of incident NAFLD (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.26; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.21–1.30), following a nonlinear exposure-response relationship. Accelerated biological aging mediated 6.5% of this association, whereas homeostatic dysregulation and allostatic load contributed modestly. Benzene exposure and polygenic risk showed no multiplicative interaction, but their cumulative effect raised NAFLD risk among highly susceptible individuals. A machine-learning model integrating benzene and covariates predicted NAFLD with good discrimination (AUC = 0.753), and an external urinary-biomarker analysis in NHANES was directionally consistent. Thus, long-term low-level benzene exposure increases incident NAFLD risk, partly through accelerated biological aging.

title: Streamlined 2D multimodal fusion framework predicts 90 day functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke
abstract: Functional outcome prediction after endovascular therapy can support early risk stratification in acute ischemic stroke. We developed a 2D multimodal fusion framework using multicenter data from 405 patients with post-interventional cerebral hyperdensity on immediate non-contrast CT. Radiomic and deep transfer learning features were extracted from the single CT slice showing the largest hyperdensity area and combined with clinical variables using an Extra Trees classifier. In the external test cohort, the fusion model predicted unfavorable 90-day outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score greater than 2, with an AUC of 0.803, specificity of 88.0%, positive predictive value of 93.3%, and sensitivity of 60.9%. SHAP analysis identified malignant cerebral edema, age, baseline NIHSS, reperfusion status, and imaging intensity descriptors as influential factors. By reducing dependence on 3D segmentation, this framework provides an early phase (within 5 days) prognostic assessment tool for individualized in-hospital risk stratification after thrombectomy.

title: Enhancing cervical squamous cell carcinoma diagnosis under distribution shift via domain-adaptive representation learning
abstract: Automated whole-slide image (WSI) analysis for cervical squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) is challenged by limited pathological specificity in general models and poor cross-center generalization. We propose CSCC-PAG (pre-training, adaptation, generalization), a framework integrating domain-specific pre-training with self-supervised domain adaptation. Utilizing 8,041 CSCC WSIs, we applied the self-supervised pre-training for CSCC (SPC) feature extractor, which significantly outperforms pan-cancer baselines in the typing, grading, and segmentation tasks. To address domain shift, we developed representative sample domain adaptation (RSDA), combining masked autoencoders (MAEs) with a k -means buffer strategy for label-free adaptation. The results demonstrate that SPC captures fine-grained CSCC morphology, while RSDA effectively recovers performance degradation across centers without requiring target-domain annotations. This study provides a comprehensive solution for automated CSCC diagnosis, covering the entire pipeline from large-scale pre-training to few-shot generalized deployment, demonstrating its immense potential for real-world clinical implementation.

title: Temporal dynamics of antennal responses encode plant stress and ecological relevance in Spodoptera littoralis moths
abstract: Polyphagous insects draw fitness-relevant information from complex plant odor blends, yet electroantennography (EAG) studies often emphasize response amplitude rather than temporal structure. We combined natural plant volatile stimuli, temporal EAG analysis, and machine-learning classification to examine the responses of male and female Spodoptera littoralis antennae to host/edible plants, non-hosts, and drought-stressed plants. EAGs entailed much information about plant volatiles. Female responses showed stronger functional organization and higher classification performance for the above-mentioned categories, particularly for non-host plants, whereas males retained discrimination only under high-contrast stress conditions. These findings suggest that peripheral antennal dynamics preserve biologically relevant information about plant suitability and physiological state. More broadly, this framework offers a new approach for linking peripheral olfactory physiology with future electrophysiological and behavioral experiments.

title: An intelligent weighted adaptive regression process for reliable and uncertainty aware drought forecasting
abstract: Accurate drought forecasting enables the management and reduction of impacts on water resources and farming systems. Hence, this research introduces a hybrid machine learning model called the weighted adaptive regression process (WARP), based on Gaussian process regression, generalized ridge regression, an adaptive mechanism to dynamically update the kernel matrix, and a feature relevance mechanism to assign weights to input variables. The model is optimized using the enhanced multi-operator Runge-Kutta algorithm. Moreover, a novel feature selection method based on kernel ridge regression and permutation importance is developed, while an enhanced multi-variate variational mode decomposition is implemented to decompose the input variables. The WARP applied to forecast SPEI at three stations in Iran outperformed LSSVM, DRVFL, and CFNN with correlation coefficient of up to 0.99 and MaxAE of 0.49. The uncertainty analysis demonstrated lower uncertainty and narrower prediction intervals confirming WARP as a reliable and promising drought forecasting approach.

title: Ultrasound-based breast nodule malignancy diagnosis using CNN enhanced by knowledge distillation
abstract: Accurate discrimination of benign and malignant breast lesions is essential for early diagnosis, yet remains challenging due to lesion heterogeneity and interobserver variability in ultrasound assessment. We developed a deep learning (DL) framework integrating dual inverted bottleneck blocks (Dual-IB), adaptive hierarchical feature fusion, and knowledge distillation (KD) for breast ultrasound lesion classification. The model was trained and evaluated on public datasets and validated on an independent external cohort to assess its generalizability. Results demonstrated superior performance compared with baseline methods and resident radiologists, while maintaining robust performance across diverse datasets and imaging conditions. On the external validation dataset, the model achieved the best performance, with an accuracy (Acc) of 92.64% and an F1-score of 92.37%. Furthermore, class activation mapping (CAM) visualizations revealed focused and anatomically plausible attention patterns within lesion regions, aiding interpretation and suggesting its potential to assist in breast ultrasound lesion classification.

title: Extending digital biology: Bacterial survival and morphological heterogeneity under antibiotic stress
abstract: Bacterial morphology is modified by antibiotic stress depending on the antibiotic mechanism of action, while changes in morphology can contribute to cell survival. Here we present a workflow that generates morphological signatures for the progeny of individual bacterial cells across 168 antibiotic conditions. The workflow uses stationary microfluidic droplets to encapsulate and grow bacteria and confocal microscopy to image the droplet content. A custom image analysis pipeline labels morphologies in a subset of images to train a neural network. The network yields multidimensional morphological signatures from 82,000 droplets, showing the co-existence of different morphologies even for the progeny of individual cells. The signatures differ with antibiotic type and concentration, providing a way to distinguish antibiotics by their mode of action. Combined with digital detection of bacterial survival within droplets, this workflow provides a quantitative platform to investigate antibiotic resistance and identify the antimicrobial activity of unknown compounds.

title: Advancing microalgae biomass cultivation for an integrated sustainable wastewater treatment and resource recovery
abstract: Microalgae have emerged as a promising bioresource for the integrated treatment of effluent, the production of biomass, and the mitigation of carbon emissions, thereby contributing to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs 7 and 13). This review summarizes the most recent developments in the management of wastewater using microalgae, with a particular focus on resource recovery and process integration. Nevertheless, challenges such as oxygen accumulation, biofouling, high energy demand, and scale-up constraints persist, despite the fact that configurations such as tubular, flat-panel, and bubble-column reactors offer flexibility across scales. Additionally, the topic of the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning is addressed in order to address process constraints by means of predictive modeling, real-time optimization, and enhanced strain and process selection. In conclusion, this review offers a concentrated viewpoint on the advancement of sustainable microalgae systems by integrating technological and biological innovations.

title: Quantum-enhanced trusted execution with dynamic policy optimization for zero-trust edge computing
abstract: Zero-trust edge computing faces escalating security challenges from quantum threats, heterogeneous resources, and dynamic operational conditions. This paper proposes Q-TEE-DSO, a collaborative architecture integrating quantum-enhanced trusted execution environments with post-quantum cryptography and reinforcement learning-based dynamic security optimization. By embedding quantum random number generation and lightweight quantum key distribution into hardware-enforced TEEs, the framework strengthens trust-root initialization and session-key establishment under quantum-aware threat models. Instruction-level optimization of lattice-based PQC algorithms, combined with enclave-aware memory isolation and side-channel mitigation, reduces cryptographic overhead on constrained edge devices. A reinforcement learning-driven DSO-Engine dynamically adapts encryption strength, access control policies, and privacy-preserving computation modes according to real-time system load and threat levels. Experimental evaluations on heterogeneous testbeds demonstrate a 37% reduction in cryptographic latency and 42% improvement in energy efficiency compared with conventional approaches, alongside 99.88% availability, robust heterogeneous compatibility, and stable long-term operation across diverse network topologies.

title: A distribution-aware semi-supervised pipeline for cost-effective neuron segmentation
abstract: ABSTRACT Semi-supervised learning offers a cost-effective approach for neuron segmentation in electron microscopy (EM) volumes. This technique leverages extensive unlabeled data to regularize supervised training for more robust predictions of neuron boundaries. However, the distribution mismatch between labeled and unlabeled data, due to limited annotations and diverse neuronal structures, can cause unreliable predictions on unlabeled data, thus limiting the generalization of semi-supervised models. In this paper, we develop a distribution-aware pipeline to address the inherent mismatch issue and enhance semi-supervised neuron segmentation in EM volumes. At the data level, we propose an unsupervised heuristic to select valuable sub-volumes as labeled data based on distribution similarity in a pretrained feature space, ensuring a representative coverage of neuronal structures. At the model level, we introduce an axial-through mixing strategy into anisotropic neuron segmentation and integrate it into a semi-supervised framework. Building on this, we establish cross-view consistency constraints through intra- and inter-mixing of labeled and unlabeled data, which facilitates the learning of shared semantics across distributions. Extensive experiments on public EM datasets from multiple species, imaging modalities, and resolutions demonstrate the effectiveness of our method. Codes and demos are available at https://github.com/yanchaoz/SL-SSNS .

title: Integration of unpaired and heterogeneous clinical flow cytometry data
abstract: We introduce the Unbiasing Variational Autoencoder (UVAE), a computational framework for the integration of unpaired biomedical data streams such as clinical flow cytometry. UVAE addresses batch effect correction and data alignment by training a semi-supervised model on partially labeled datasets, enabling simultaneous normalization and integration of diverse data within a shared latent space. The framework implements a probabilistic model for batch effect normalization and balances class contents during training to ensure accurate representation of underlying cell composition. We apply UVAE to integrate heterogeneous clinical flow cytometry data from COVID-19 patients. The integrated data enhances the statistical signal of cell types associated with disease severity, enables clustering of subpopulations without the impediment of batch effects, and improves the performance of longitudinal regression for predicting peak disease severity from temporal patient samples.

title: Hybrid multiscale forecasting of SRU sulfur gas concentrations using VMD CEEMDAN and optimized PatchTST
abstract: The sulfur recovery process in SRUs is highly nonlinear and non-stationary, making accurate forecasting of H 2 S and SO 2 concentrations challenging yet crucial for efficient, low-carbon operation. Many existing models fail to handle multi-scale fluctuations, high-frequency noise, and complex variable couplings, limiting their accuracy. This study presents a multi-scale framework combining variational mode decomposition (VMD), complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (CEEMDAN), an enhanced patch time-series transformer with ProbSparse attention (PatchTST-PSA), and projection iterative modeling optimization (PIMO). VMD decomposes the concentration series into intrinsic mode functions, and CEEMDAN suppresses noise while preserving dynamics. PatchTST-PSA captures nonlinear variable interactions, while PIMO optimizes hyperparameters. Experiments on SRU data from an Italian refinery demonstrate that the framework provides improved results in RMSE, MAE, MAPE, and R 2 compared to six baseline models, highlighting its robustness and industrial relevance.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution and driving mechanism of synergistic carbon and pollution reduction
abstract: Climate change and environmental pollution are key global challenges, with synergistic carbon-pollution reduction a global consensus. As the world's largest developing economy and carbon emitter, China's experience informs global synergistic governance. Spatiotemporal evolution and driving mechanisms of synergistic carbon and pollution reduction from 297 Chinese cities (2000-2023) are examined, applying the coupling coordination degree, k-means clustering, difference-in-differences, and moderating effect models. Findings show that the national coupling coordination degree of synergistic carbon and pollution reduction (CCD-SCPR) exhibits an inverted U-shaped dynamic evolution and gradient spatial differentiation. The "core-periphery" clustering pattern is found, with nearly half of the cities remaining in a dilemma of low CCD-SCPR, underscoring the urgency of synergistic governance. Data element marketization significantly improves CCD-SCPR by breaking information barriers, optimizing resource allocation, and empowering technological innovation. It forms a positive moderating effect with environmental regulation, yielding extra governance benefits. Proposals include differentiated strategies, innovative urban governance, optimized policy coordination, and deeper data element reforms.

title: An efficient framework for protein-protein interaction prediction by integrating stacked denoising autoencoders and random ferns
abstract: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) are crucial for understanding disease and discovering drug targets. To overcome the limitations of experimental methods, we propose SDAERFs, a computational framework that predicts PPIs from protein sequences. It leverages evolutionary information in position-specific scoring matrices (PSSMs), employs a stacked denoising autoencoder (SDAE) for feature extraction, and uses a Random Ferns (RFs) classifier for prediction. Extensive validation on benchmark datasets yielded high accuracies of 98.13% and 98.60%. Comprehensive comparisons confirmed the model's superior performance. SDAERFs provides an efficient and reliable tool for advancing PPI prediction and therapeutic development.

title: Divergent behavioral strategies in Wistar and Wistar-Kyoto rats in a naturalistic task reveal mood disorder phenotypes
abstract: Rodent models are essential for studying mood disorders, yet many assays rely on methods that may not reflect natural behavior. Food hoarding offers an ethologically relevant paradigm integrating reward seeking, risk assessment, and safety-seeking strategies. We assessed hoarding in Wistar-Kyoto (Kyoto) rats, a model of depression and anxiety, compared with Wistar controls. Kyoto rats, particularly females, displayed robust hoarding, frequently transporting all food items to the safe base while consuming little. In contrast, Wistars consumed more and showed greater exploratory activity, moving at higher velocity. Principal component analysis and k-means clustering identified distinct behavioral phenotypes, with Kyotos clustered into high hoarding, low exploratory profiles consistent with anxiety- or depressive-like profiles, while Wistars clustered into more exploratory phenotypes. Pose estimation revealed reduced locomotor velocity in Kyoto rats compared with Wistar controls, consistent with altered risk assessment. Overall, this task captures strain- and individual-level variation in mood-related behavior under more naturalistic conditions.

title: Longitudinal multicohort evidence for bidirectional diabetes arthritis links in older adults
abstract: Diabetes mellitus and arthritis frequently co-occur in older adults, but whether they causally reinforce each other and through which mechanisms remain unclear. We used harmonized longitudinal data from three nationally representative cohorts across China (CHARLS), the United States (HRS), and Europe (SHARE) to test bidirectional relationships between diabetes and arthritis in late life. Cross-lagged panel models over multiple waves quantified reciprocal effects, prespecified mediation analyses evaluated 21 biologically and clinically motivated mediators, and the NOTEARS algorithm probed data-driven causal network structure. Across all cohorts, diabetes consistently increased subsequent arthritis risk and to a lesser extent, arthritis increased subsequent diabetes risk, with effects robust across demographic and clinical subgroups. C-reactive protein, grip strength, and HbA1c emerged as the dominant mediators, linking metabolic, inflammatory, and functional pathways. These findings support viewing diabetes and arthritis as mutually reinforcing conditions that share modifiable upstream mechanisms, motivating integrated prevention and management strategies in aging populations.

title: An intelligent framework for advancing large-scale omics data integration
abstract: Clinical and biological insights from large-scale omics data are often limited by technical variability and analytical complexity. Here, we present BioinAI, a comprehensive framework that integrates an intelligent system with two algorithms, DeepAdvancer and stNiche, to enable effective data integration. Specifically, DeepAdvancer leverages a class-aware adversarial autoencoder to reconstruct gene expression profiles. When applied to 49,738 samples across 1,016 datasets, it uncovered a transcriptomic continuum and differential trajectory axes, which link diverse diseases through shared immune responses and distinct fate determinants. In the spatial context, stNiche leverages graph networks and symmetry-aware matching to identify functional cellular niches across heterogeneous slides. For instance, it identified a fibroblast-immune niche surrounding hair follicles in healthy skin that is lost in pathological states. BioinAI also provides an online conversational analysis platform, powered by multiple semi-agents, facilitating biological insight extraction from transcriptomic data.

title: A high-power plantar energy harvester with LSTM-KAN adaptive damping control
abstract: Here within enclosed is our paper for consideration to be published on “Energy Conversion and Management”. The further information about the paper is in the following:Plantar energy harvesters demonstrate significant potential for continuously powering portable electronic devices. However, low output power and poor wearing comfort remain critical challenges hindering the practical deployment of plantar energy harvesters. This paper proposes a novel adaptive-damping, high-power plantar energy harvester (DPEH) utilizing a hybrid Long Short-Term Memory- Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (LSTM-KAN) architecture to address these effectively. A bidirectionally extensible cross-beam array structure with spatial compression capability is designed, combined with pulley block-belt composite transmission system. It achieves a 17.6-fold stroke amplification, improving the power output of the DPEH significantly. Furthermore, a hybrid LSTM-KAN framework was developed to recognize speed of movement in real-time during walking and running. The identified gait parameters dynamically modulate electromagnetic damping in the DPEH, optimizing comfort-power tradeoffs. Experimental results demonstrate that a 75kg tester wearing the DPEH generated a peak power of 20.81 W and an average power of 2.75 W while running at 7 km/h. The hybrid recognition model achieved 99.84% accuracy across locomotion states and speeds, with ergonomic comfort improved by 12%. This strategy establishes a new framework paradigm for self-regulating human-machine cooperative energy systems.

title: Climate-adaptive and low-carbon multi-objective water resources optimization in arid oasis cities
abstract: To address the intensifying water supply-demand imbalance in arid regions under climate change and low-carbon development, this study uses Shihezi City, Xinjiang, as a case study. CMIP6 climate data were used to drive an LSTM model for basin-scale runoff projection, and a multi-objective water resources optimization framework was developed by integrating NSGA-III with CRITIC-TOPSIS, considering water shortage, economic benefits, pollutant emissions, and water-use carbon emissions. Results show that future runoff in the Manas River Basin generally declines, with the most pronounced reduction in September; by 2030, water scarcity in Shihezi City remains substantial. The optimal scheme under SSP1-2.6 performs well in water conservation and carbon reduction; SSP2-4.5 balances economic development and environmental protection, whereas SSP5-8.5 delivers higher economic benefits but greater environmental pressure. The results provide support for efficient water resources allocation and low-carbon utilization in arid oasis cities.

title: Large-scale circulation shapes the spatial organization of anomalous precipitation over Northern Jiangsu
abstract: Anomalous precipitation events often exhibit coherent spatial organization rather than isolated intensity extremes, reshaping regional flood risk in subtropical monsoon zones. Using 1-km daily precipitation data from 1961 to 2019, we developed an unsupervised framework combining a convolutional autoencoder and a self-organizing map to identify event-scale anomalous precipitation patterns over Northern Jiangsu. A total of 543 anomalous days were classified into five distinct spatial types characterized by pronounced north-south contrasts and east-west differentiation. Interaction analysis reveals suppressive and co-occurring relationships among patterns, indicating structured atmospheric control. Phase variations of the Western North Pacific Subtropical High and the East Asian jet significantly modulate the probability of different patterns. Incorporating circulation-conditioned pattern probabilities into runoff forecasting improves peak discharge simulation. These findings highlight the importance of circulation-structured precipitation in linking atmospheric variability with hydrological response under nonstationary climate conditions.

title: Bioengineering advances in pancreatic cancer organoids for reproducible tumor microenvironment modeling
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains lethal due to late-stage diagnosis and limited non-surgical treatment options. Its intratumoral heterogeneity and desmoplastic tumor microenvironment (TME) drive invasion, immune escape, and treatment failure. Patient-derived organoids (PDOs) have emerged as efficient model platforms for simulating the TME and preserving tumor heterogeneity and enabling functional testing in vitro ; however, conventional PDO cultures lack defined and controllable microenvironmental components and often exhibited limited reproducibility, physiological fidelity, and observability. This review synthesizes recent bioengineering advances that upgrade pancreatic cancer PDO platforms across three interconnected dimensions: (1) engineered extracellular matrices and biofabrication for reproducible construction; (2) co-culture, microfluidic, and bioreactor systems for physiological fidelity; (3) imaging AI and biosensor pipelines for quantitative monitoring. We highlight practical design principles and remaining bottlenecks for standardization, scalability, and clinical translation.

title: Q-AVOA-net: A multi-domain, quantum-inspired feature-selection and deep-fuzzy framework for interpretable white blood cell classification
abstract: Accurate white blood cell (WBC) classification is crucial for hematological diagnostics, yet current automated systems struggle with data imbalance, limited generalization, and lack of explainability. This paper proposes Q-AVOA-Net, a quantum-inspired multi-domain framework that enhances WBC subtype classification accuracy, interpretability, and robustness. The model integrates: (i) Enhanced Contourlet Transform with learnable Gabor filters for multi-scale directional representation, (ii) Bi-LSTM Attention for hierarchical sequential learning, (iii) Quantum-inspired African Vulture Optimization Algorithm (Q-AVOA) for multi-objective feature selection, and (iv) an interpretable fuzzy decision layer for calibrated predictions. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets (Raabin, LISC, BCCD) demonstrate Q-AVOA-Net achieves 96.8% accuracy, 96.5% F1-score, and 0.991 AUC while reducing feature dimensionality by 38% and inference time by 22% compared to hybrid CNN-Transformer baselines. The framework also reduces Expected Calibration Error by ≈52%, significantly improving confidence estimation and clinical reliability. Q-AVOA-Net provides a robust, interpretable, and computationally efficient solution for next-generation hematological analysis and diagnostic decision support.

title: Development of CNN and LSTM fusion model for early fault warning in hydro turbine units
abstract: Early fault detection is important for the safe and stable operation of large hydro turbine units under complex and variable operating conditions. This study develops an early fault warning framework for high dimensional multisource monitoring data by integrating Kendall rank correlation-based parameter grouping, systematic data governance, sparse principal component analysis, and a CNN LSTM prediction model. Fifty two operating parameters are organized into six groups and transformed into six sparse state features. The CNN LSTM model captures local correlations and temporal evolution, achieving R 2 values of 0.947, 0.955, 0.848, 0.701, 0.687, and 0.853 for SPCA1 to SPCA6. Prediction residuals combined with 2σ and 3σ thresholds identify early degradation before the recorded fault, with warning lead times of up to 33 time steps. The framework provides a practical approach for condition monitoring and hierarchical early warning of large hydro turbine units.

title: Comorbidity patterns and sex differences in late-onset Alzheimer’s disease using electronic records
abstract: In this retrospective study, we applied unsupervised learning techniques to electronic medical records from the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) to characterize Alzheimer's disease (AD) comorbidity patterns. Given the well-known female predominance in AD, we performed sex-stratified analyses to explore differences in comorbidity patterns based on sex. Findings were evaluated using an independent UC-wide dataset. Among 8,363 patients in the UCSF dataset, we observed five data-driven comorbidity clusters related to cardiovascular conditions, gastrointestinal disorders, and frailty-related conditions such as pneumonia and pressure ulcers, as well as groups with higher and lower overall comorbidity burden. Sex-stratified analyses within clusters identified variation in comorbidity patterns, including circulatory diseases in males in cluster 2 and bladder stones in females in cluster 3. Key results demonstrate partial consistency in the UC-wide dataset. Our study provides a structured characterization of comorbidity heterogeneity in AD and highlights sex-related differences, though findings should be interpreted as descriptive and hypothesis-generating.

title: PyFCG: A Python toolkit for constructionist language processing and learning
abstract: This article introduces PyFCG, an open-source scientific software toolkit that enables its users to efficiently integrate state-of-the-art constructionist language processing and learning into larger Python projects. The toolkit provides a fully Pythonic interface to the leading computational construction grammar framework, Fluid Construction Grammar (FCG), facilitating its swift integration with Python's rich ecosystem of libraries, in particular those implementing today's most popular machine learning techniques. Apart from a general description of the toolkit, this article provides three illustrative case studies that demonstrate how PyFCG facilitates (i) the formalization and computational operationalization of construction grammar analyses, (ii) the learning of usage-based construction grammars from corpora of language use, and (iii) the implementation of multi-agent emergent communication experiments that combine symbolic and neural computation.

title: LKMHCpan: Transformer-optimized HLA-I pseudo-sequences enhance neoantigen prediction for immunotherapy
abstract: Accurate peptide-HLA class I binding prediction is fundamental for identifying tumor neoantigens and advancing personalized immunotherapy. We present LKMHCpan, a pan-specific predictor that leverages transformer networks to optimize HLA-I pseudo-sequences representation through attention-guided integration of 88 key residues primarily within the α1, α2, and α3 domains. LKMHCpan achieves a mean precision-recall area under the curve (PR-AUC) of 0.93, generalizes robustly to untrained HLA-I alleles, and supports peptides longer than 11 amino acids. In Tumor Neoantigen Selection Alliance (TESLA) data, LKMHCpan identified 94% of immunogenic neoantigens with strong score-immunogenicity correlation. Neoantigen burden from LKMHCpan significantly stratified clinical outcomes in two immunotherapy-treated cohorts: metastatic melanoma ( n  = 73) and lung cancer ( n  = 309), with high-burden patients exhibiting clinical benefit. Its ability to resolve binding motifs for untrained alleles and single-amino-acid HLA-I mutants highlights its potential for elucidating complex peptide-major histocompatibility complex (MHC) interactions. LKMHCpan provides a scalable framework for neoantigen discovery and prognostic assessment in precision immunotherapy.

title: Adaptive gating-based fusion of sequential and local features for predicting drug-drug interactions
abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-drug interactions (DDIs) is important for reducing risks associated with polypharmacy and adverse drug reactions. To overcome the limitations of experimental methods, we present AGSL-DDI, an end-to-end framework that learns interaction representations directly from SMILES sequences. Character-level embeddings are processed in parallel by a bidirectional long short-term memory network and a one-dimensional convolutional neural network to capture complementary global sequential dependencies and local chemical patterns. An adaptive gating mechanism dynamically integrates these features, while bidirectional multi-head cross-attention models fine-grained interactions between paired drugs. On the BioSNAP and DrugBank datasets, AGSL-DDI achieved AUROC values of 0.9852 and 0.9816 and AUPR values of 0.9837 and 0.9818, respectively. These results show that coordinated global-local representation learning and cross-drug interaction modeling can effectively characterize DDI patterns, providing a practical computational approach for medication risk screening and drug development.

title: Intra-DNA k-mer conservation patterns encode evolutionary selection of variants
abstract: Current approaches to variant effect prediction center on protein function and interspecies conservation, largely ignoring cues embedded in local nucleotide composition. We developed kGain, a metric that quantifies how a point mutation reshapes oligonucleotide frequency relative to the host genome. In  Escherichia coli  and  Saccharomyces cerevisiae  long-term evolution data, fixed, essential-gene, and recurrent mutations carry elevated kGain values that grow more pronounced over successive generations. Parallel trends appear in SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern and in a bottleneck resistance experiment, where a high-kGain  fusA  Y515N change conferred antibiotic resistance at no detectable fitness cost. A transformer regressor trained on one strain transfers accurately to others, indicating that the compositional rules kGain captures are broadly conserved and offering a new sequence-intrinsic dimension for understanding adaptive selection.

title: ShapeUpLMD: Automated spatial optimization of laser microdissection for tissue sampling
abstract: Laser microdissection (LMD) enables enrichment of defined cellular populations from heterogeneous tissues but lacks standardized approaches for generating optimized regions of interest (ROIs) for scalable spatial multi-omic workflows. We developed ShapeUpLMD, an open-source tool that optimizes digitally annotated ROIs for automated spatial LMD workflows. Uterine serous carcinoma tumor ( n = 11) tissue sections were pathologist-annotated, and tumor-specific HALO classifier-generated ROIs were refined by ShapeUpLMD and collected using a Leica LMD7. Classifier-estimated tumor ROIs increased effective tumor purity by 86 ± 6% relative to whole tissue while maintaining strong concordance between predicted and collected regions (accuracy = 0.90 ± 0.05). Data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry quantified upwards of 6,500 proteins, revealing regionally coherent clustering and patterns consistent with tumor and non-tumor cell admixture. ShapeUpLMD provides an automated, scalable framework linking digital pathology with high-fidelity LMD for standardized spatial multi-omic profiling. ShapeUpLMD is freely available at https://github.com/GYNCOE/ShapeUpLMD.

title: When artificial intelligence falls short: Multimodal analysis improves head and neck lymphoma classification
authors: Cinthia Veronica Bardález López de Cáceres
abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly applied in digital pathology, yet its generalizability in routine diagnostic settings remains challenging. We developed a multimodal framework for classifying head and neck lymphoid lesions using 610 cases from ten institutions. UNI was used for histological feature extraction, while CellViT++ enabled nuclear segmentation and quantitative morphometry, subsequently integrated with clinicopathological variables. The UNI-based model showed limited generalization (accuracy of 0.66, F1 score of 0.65, and Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.66), whereas multimodal integration substantially improved internal performance (accuracy of 0.91, F1 score of 0.91, and AUROC of 0.87) and maintained performance across two external cohorts (accuracy of 0.84 and 0.79 and AUROC of 0.84 and 0.80). Class-stratified SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis revealed distinct feature attribution patterns across diagnostic groups, with nuclear morphometric features contributing prominently to model predictions. Morphology alone imposes a clear performance ceiling in head and neck lymphomas. Multimodal integration provides a more reliable and clinically relevant approach, supporting diagnostic triage in routine practice.

title: A deep learning model for flood forecasting based on dynamic lag encoding and multi-head attention
abstract: Conventional flood forecasting models often struggle to effectively capture the time-lag characteristics of rainfall-runoff responses within a basin, and their decision-making processes generally lack interpretability. This study used 19 years (1979-1997) of multi-station rainfall and outlet discharge data from the Hydrological Yearbook of the Yellow River Basin, and selected 53 representative flood events from the Huangfuchuan Basin for model development and evaluation. A deep learning flood forecasting model (D-TMA-LSTM) was developed by integrating dynamic lag encoding with a multi-head attention mechanism. The results show that D-TMA-LSTM outperformed the original LSTM and D-LSTM across forecast lead times from t+1 to t+6. At t+1, NSE, KGE, and R 2  values were 0.959, 0.934, and 0.964, respectively, while RMSE decreased by 31.74%. The model also maintained stable performance at t+6, providing an effective framework for flood forecasting in basins with complex rainfall-runoff lag responses.

title: Bundled AI supported automated breast ultrasound versus handheld ultrasound in organized screening in China
abstract: Evidence for AI-supported ultrasound screening programs remains limited. We compared a bundled AI-supported automated breast ultrasound (ABUS) workflow with handheld ultrasound (HHUS) in a government-organized screening program. Adjusted risk ratios accounted for baseline imbalance, and standardized cancer detection rate (CDR) accounted for differential biopsy completion. ABUS reduced recall (12.1% vs. 29.9%; adjusted RR 0.45 [95% CI 0.42-0.48]) and biopsy recall (0.99% vs. 2.19%; adjusted RR 0.50 [0.39-0.64]), while increasing biopsy positive predictive value (PPV; 62.1% vs. 20.0%; adjusted RR 2.46 [1.34-4.52]). Observed CDR was higher but not statistically significant (3.08 vs. 1.22 per 1000; adjusted rate ratios 1.90 [0.94-3.86]). Early-stage proportion was higher with ABUS but not statistically significant (84.8% vs. 50.0%; adjusted RR 1.64 [0.71-3.80]). The bundled ABUS pathway was associated with substantially lower recall and higher biopsy PPV. Findings for cancer detection and stage distribution were exploratory because of differential biopsy completion and the small number of cancers.

title: Epidemic waves and cytokine signatures of seven respiratory pathogens after COVID-19 restrictions
abstract: Non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) during COVID-19 reduced population exposure to respiratory pathogens, creating population-level immunity debt. After these measures were lifted in China in May 2023, acute respiratory infections resurged with altered age distributions and co-infection dynamics. We conducted 20-month surveillance of 54,902 febrile patients and measured 47 plasma analytes in a nested cohort ( n = 187). Three sequential epidemic waves emerged: SARS-CoV-2 (July–August 2024), influenza A virus (IAV; December 2024–March 2025), and IAV plus human rhinovirus (November 2025–January 2026), with a 9.5% co-infection rate. G-CSF and IL-1Ra were elevated across all pathogens and tracked with clinical severity, whereas IAV-associated IL-4 elevation was severity-independent. A five-cytokine random forest classifier discriminated pathogen groups with 87.3% cross-validated accuracy. Pathogen-characteristic cytokine profiles may support etiological inference from single plasma samples and inform precision-medicine approaches to respiratory infections, pending external validation.

title: Individual differences in sequential decision-making
abstract: People differ widely in how they make decisions in uncertain environments. While many studies leverage this variability to measure differences in specific cognitive processes and parameters, the key dimension(s) of individual variability in uncertain decision-making tasks has not been identified. Here, we analyzed behavioral data from 1,001 participants performing a restless three-armed bandit task, where reward probabilities fluctuated unpredictably over time. Using a novel analytical approach that controlled for the stochasticity in this task, we identified a dominant nonlinear axis of individual variability. We found that this primary axis of variability was strongly and selectively correlated with the probability of exploration, as inferred by latent state modeling. This suggests that the major factor shaping individual differences in bandit task performance is the tendency to explore (versus exploit), rather than reinforcement learning model parameters, personality characteristics, or low-level strategies. Certain demographic characteristics also predicted variance along this principal axis: participants at the exploratory end tended to be younger than participants at the exploitative end, and self-identified men were overrepresented at both extremes. Together, these findings offer a principled framework for understanding individual differences in task behavior while highlighting the cognitive and demographic factors that shape individual differences in decision-making under uncertainty.

title: CASCADE is an agentic AI framework for trustworthy biomarker discovery in precision oncology
abstract: Autonomous AI agents can now run end-to-end scientific analyses, yet no general method ensures those analyses are correct, and one upstream error can propagate across hundreds of downstream results at machine speed. We present CASCADE, an agentic validation framework built on mandatory, quantitatively gated analytical steps. Its central principle, specification-implementation separation, fixes what must be validated and to what standard while leaving how to the agent, so conclusions depend on the protocol rather than the model executing it. Every analysis is preserved as human-readable code with a complete decision log. Derived from a ∼25,000-patient clinical cancer genomics cohort and applied unmodified across three settings (13,424 patients), CASCADE recovered established signal, reported insufficient power instead of a false result where data were inadequate, and reversed a clinically consequential artifact (hazard ratio 0.84, corrected to 1.25). Findings were replicated in two independent multi-institutional cohorts, and three AI systems reproduced them with high fidelity.

title: Zebrafish sleep displays distinct sub-states
abstract: Sleep is an essential and evolutionarily-conserved behavior. While mammals and several other species have been shown to exhibit well-defined sleep sub-states, some of which have been ascribed specific functions, it remains unclear to what extent such differentiation exists across the animal kingdom. Here we show, using long-term behavioral data combined with Hidden Markov Modeling, that larval zebrafish display distinct deep and light sleep sub-states. Although both states occur primarily at night, fish respond differently to sleep deprivation and arousing stimuli depending on which sleep sub-state they are in. Moreover, the proportions of deep and light sleep are selectively altered by genetic and pharmacological manipulations of melatonin, serotonin, and norepinephrine signaling, offering new insights into how these neuromodulators shape sleep architecture. These results support zebrafish as a tractable model for dissecting the regulation and function of sleep sub-states. More broadly, they demonstrate that structured, multi-state sleep is a conserved feature of vertebrate behavior.

title: Coordinated immune response distinguishes duration of SARS-CoV-2 viral particle shedding in humans
abstract: = 223). While PVS participants demonstrated lower overall SARS-CoV-2-specific antibody magnitudes, over-representation analysis revealed that immune feature magnitude alone could not fully explain cohort differences. Hierarchical clustering and network analyses identified more highly coordinated antibody responses, T cell activation, and Fc-mediated function among non-PVS compared to PVS participants. These findings link control of viral antigen shedding to a coordinated immune response.

title: Opioid receptor distribution in the claustrum-dorsal endopiriform complex
abstract: Abstract The claustrum and dorsal endopiriform regions form a thin subcortical sheet reciprocally connected to the neocortex that is enriched in opioid receptors. The precise cellular distribution of opioid receptors within this region remains unclear. Using multiplexed fluorescence in situ hybridization (mFISH) and hierarchical cluster analysis, we mapped the expression of mu ( Oprm ), delta ( Oprd ), kappa ( Oprk ), and ORL1 ( Oprl ) opioid receptor genes at single-cell resolution in the mouse claustrum-dorsal endopiriform. Among 2,269 neurons analyzed, six transcriptional clusters were identified: three excitatory (CLA, CLA/OPRK, cortical excitatory) and three inhibitory (SST, PVALB, broad inhibitory). Oprk expression was uniquely restricted to excitatory claustrum neurons and particularly enriched in the CLA/OPRK cluster which was comprised largely of Synpr + claustrum core projection cells. In contrast, Oprd, Oprm , and Oprl genes were more broadly distributed across both excitatory and inhibitory populations, with Oprd enriched in parvalbumin ( Pvalb) inhibitory neurons and Oprl in somatostatin ( Sst) inhibitory neurons. Spatial mapping confirmed that Oprk expressing cells were concentrated within the claustrum core, whereas other receptor subtypes extended across the entire claustrum and into adjacent cortical regions. A comparable distribution of opioid receptors was observed in the neighbouring dorsal endopiriform. Analysis of a publicly available single cell sequencing dataset of the macaque claustrum also revealed a similar receptor distribution, where Oprk expression was enriched within a subset of excitatory projection neurons, and Oprm,Oprd , and Oprl expressed widely in both inhibitory and excitatory cells. Together, these findings demonstrate an evolutionarily conserved, cell-type-specific organization of opioid receptor expression in the claustrum-dorsal endopiriform. These results indicate that kappa opioid receptor expression is a defining molecular feature of excitatory claustrum projection neurons and suggest distinct roles for other opioid receptors in modulating inhibitory and cortical circuits.

title: Slow intrinsic oscillations in the ventrolateral preoptic nucleus
abstract: Abstract The ventrolateral preoptic nucleus (VLPO) of the hypothalamus plays a major role in the induction and consolidation of non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep. While VLPO neurons are heterogeneous, they often display low-threshold spikes (LTS), a feature that supports rhythmic activity. Nevertheless, rhythmic bursting in these VLPO neurons has never been observed. Here, we report that ∼12% of VLPO neurons in a large database of ex vivo patch-clamp recordings display spontaneous rhythmic bursting of action potentials. This activity occurred in putative sleep-promoting neurons, identified by inhibitory responses to noradrenaline (NA), as well as wake-active neurons that were activated by NA. Unsupervised clustering of 24 neurons based on burst properties, electrophysiological, and morphological features revealed three distinct groups: one corresponding to putative sleep-promoting neurons and two wake-active neurons with fast and slow bursting dynamics. Strikingly, membrane potential oscillations persisted in the presence of tetrodotoxin (TTX), indicating that rhythmic bursting is driven by intrinsic mechanisms rather than network activity. These findings suggest that rhythmic bursting is an intrinsic and functionally relevant mode of activity in VLPO neurons, which may contribute to sleep regulation.

title: Awake cortex stabilizes traveling waves for global and reliable information routing
abstract: How does the brain organize neural information for perception during wakefulness, yet lose such organization under anesthesia? Theories on consciousness hypothesize that perceptual experience arises from global communication across the cerebral cortex. However, the neural substrate that mediates information transfer between cortical regions remains uncertain. Here, developing large-scale and high-density electrocorticography arrays, we demonstrated that traveling waves serve as a fundamental mode for global information transfer. Compared with the anesthetized state, visual-evoked traveling waves during wakefulness exhibited greater stability. Hierarchical clustering uncovered the emergence of widespread waves with a rich repertoire of motifs only in the awake state. By quantifying the fidelity of information routing, we found that information flows more reliably along the direction of wave propagation during wakefulness than under anesthesia. This study provides meso- and macroscopic evidence consistent with theories of consciousness and introduces a framework, informational tuning , for characterizing the geometrical relations between neural and informational flows.

title: Multi-region brain transcriptomes uncover two subtypes of aging individuals with differences in Alzheimer risk and the impact of APOEε4
abstract: Abstract The heterogeneity of the older population suggests the existence of subsets of individuals which share certain brain molecular features and respond differently to risk factors for Alzheimer’s disease, but this population structure remains poorly defined. Here, we performed an unsupervised clustering of individuals with multi-region brain transcriptomes to assess whether a broader approach, simultaneously considering data from multiple regions involved in cognition would uncover such subsets. We implemented a canonical correlation-based analysis in a Discovery cohort of 459 participants from two longitudinal studies of cognitive aging that have RNA sequence profiles in three brain regions. 690 additional participants that have data in only one or two of these regions were used in the Replication effort. These clustering analyses identified two meta-clusters, MC-1 and MC-2. The two sets of participants differ primarily in their trajectories of cognitive decline, with MC-2 having a delay of 3 years to the median age of incident dementia. This is due, in part, to a greater impact of tau pathology on neuronal chromatin architecture and to broader brain changes including greater loss of white matter integrity in MC-1. Further evidence of biological differences includes a significantly larger impact of APOEε4 risk on cognitive decline in MC-1. These findings suggest that our proposed population structure captures an aspect of the more distributed molecular state of the aging brain that either enhances the effect of risk factors in MC-1 or of protective effects in MC-2. These observations may inform the design of therapeutic development efforts and of trials as both become increasingly more targeted molecularly. One Sentence Summary: There are two types of aging brains, with one being more vulnerable to APOEε4 and subsequent neuronal dysfunction and cognitive loss.

title: Network-based characterization of latent co-testing patterns in antimicrobial susceptibility testing
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance depends on antimicrobial susceptibility testing, yet antibiotic panels vary by pathogen cohort, specimen, year, ward, and care setting. We term these empirically reconstructed testing architectures shadow antibiograms: structures that shape which susceptibility results enter surveillance datasets and which resistance relationships can be observed. We analyzed approximately 13 million bacterial isolates from Germany's National Antibiotic Resistance Surveillance system (2019-2023) across six WHO BPPL-aligned operational cohorts. Co-testing networks were constructed using Jaccard, Dice, cosine, and phi-coefficient similarity, evaluated with Fisher's exact tests and Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and partitioned with multi-resolution Louvain community detection. Networks contained three to four dominant co-testing communities; false discovery rate (FDR) retention ranged from 89 to 100% across cohorts and specimen types. Jaccard provided the best balance of coherence, stability, antimicrobial-class alignment, interpretability, and edge retention. This work provides one of the first national-scale empirical characterizations of shadow antibiogram structure, supporting diagnostic stewardship and bias-aware AMR surveillance interpretation.

title: Microenvironment shapes Staphylococcus aureus phenotypes in children with cystic fibrosis over time
abstract: Abstract Staphylococcus aureus (SA) is a common pathogen in children with cystic fibrosis (CF), frequently preceding or coexisting with Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PA). However, the extent to which its phenotypic traits are shaped by transient changes in the airway microenvironment, including coinfection and antibiotic exposure, remains poorly understood. In this study, we characterized 546 SA isolates from a longitudinal cohort of 16 pediatric CF patients over 18 months. Based on clinical records, patients were classified as SA-monoinfected or SA-PA-coinfected. Isolates were analyzed for staphyloxanthin production, hemolytic activity, DNase activity, biofilm formation, resistance to PA. Using principal component and hierarchical cluster analyses, we identified three phenotypic clusters. Isolates from monoinfected patients were predominantly found in a cluster characterized by high pigment and biofilm production and absence of chronic PA infection. In contrast, transient PA detection was associated with a shift toward a cluster displaying reduced pigment and biofilm levels. Additionally, in two out of five monoinfected patients, this shift coincided with ciprofloxacin eradication treatment including inhaled tobramycin or colistin and was accompanied by a significant increase in methicillin-resistant SA (MRSA) isolates. No phenotypic transitions were observed in chronically coinfected patients. Molecular characterization of a set of isolates showed on the one hand heterogeneity in the SA lineages and on the other hand the phenotypic profile was not determined by the genetic background. In vitro experiments showed a higher survival of MRSA over MSSA isolates in presence of both PA and ciprofloxacin. These results suggest that the phenotypic adaptation of SA in pediatric CF airway is driven by microenvironment rather than clonal background, and that transient coinfection and antibiotic exposure can favor MRSA emergence even in early-stage disease.

title: Spatial transcriptomics profiling across tissue boundaries in the developing mouse brain
abstract: Tissue boundaries preserve structural integrity and guide cell differentiation during development, despite constant stress from proliferation, cell death, and tissue deformation. To study gene regulation in these regions we developed REBOSEP, a workflow for analyzing spatial transcriptomics data to detect tissue boundaries and measure gene expression relative to boundary distance. REBOSEP uses hierarchical clustering to uncover shared regulatory patterns among genes, revealing highly diverse expression changes that can shift sharply across just a few cell layers. Using this approach, the study generated the first resource of gene expression across tissue boundaries, covering five brain-meninges boundaries in the developing mouse brain. Analysis of the dorsal pallium-meninges boundary showed specific regulatory patterns in outer brain and meningeal layers, with strong links to developmental processes and distance-dependent regulation in major pathways, including those involved in neurodevelopmental disease and cancer. Overall, REBOSEP provides a systematic framework for studying gene expression regulation at tissue boundaries.

title: Integrated multi-omics reveals methylation-linked biological heterogeneity in intermediate-risk pediatric acute myeloid leukemia
abstract: Intermediate-risk (IR) pediatric acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is clinically heterogeneous and lacks robust molecular stratification. We integrated DNA methylation, whole-exome, and transcriptome profiling in pediatric IR-AML. Unsupervised clustering of methylation profiles identified three stable epitypes (E1-E3) with distinct biological programs: E1 showed enrichment of stress-response and inflammatory pathways, E2 showed proliferative and survival signaling, and E3 showed transcriptional and developmental regulation with global hypomethylation. Despite heterogeneous mutational profiles, pathways converged across epitypes, indicating distinct genetic routes to shared functional outcomes. Immune activation was concordant across transcriptomic and epigenetic layers, with epitype-dependent variation in magnitude. Epitypes were associated with survival, with E1 showing poorer outcomes than E2 and E3. Projection onto an independent pediatric AML cohort showed partial conservation of epitype-associated methylation programs. These findings suggest that epigenetic stratification can capture clinically relevant heterogeneity beyond conventional genomic classification.

title: Behavioral ontogeny in a pelagic tunicate reveals developmental maturation and context-dependent modulation
abstract: ABSTRACT Behavioral developmental plasticity refers to the lasting changes in an organism’s behavior that occur during development in response to external and internal cues, enhancing survival and reproduction. While well studied in vertebrates, its occurrence in other chordates, including tunicates, the closest relatives of vertebrates, remains unclear. We built a behavioral atlas of the planktonic tunicate Oikopleura dioica across its life cyclefrom larval to adult stages using high-throughput tracking and unsupervised analysis. Swimming kinematics, exploration, and thigmotaxis increased with development. Adults exhibit a unique innovation, known as the house, a complex extracellular filtration structure encasing the animal trunk, which drastically alters locomotion and exploration compared to free-swimming individuals. Postural variation during ontogeny is captured by seven basic shapes (“eigenoikopleuras”), with complex shapes becoming more frequent over time. Spatiotemporal embedding and Hidden Markov modeling revealed that behavioral refinement arises from changes in motor modules and their transitions. House occupancy similarly shifts these modules, indicating context-specific specialization. This continuous behavioral maturation parallels Oikopleura ’s neotenic morphology, retaining a larval body plan unlike other tunicates. Our atlas provides a quantitative framework for exploring the evolution of behavioral developmental plasticity in chordates.

title: SLC39A10 drives M2 macrophage polarization and gastric cancer progression through the MAPK14(p38α) pathway
abstract: Background: Gastric cancer (GC) continues to significantly contribute to global cancer mortality, with disease progression driven by complex interactions between tumor cells and microenvironmental factors. Emerging evidence implicates zinc metabolism as a key regulator of oncogenic signaling pathways, particularly through the zinc transporter SLC39A10, which promotes tumor proliferation. While SLC39A10 has been linked to gastric carcinogenesis, its precise molecular mechanisms involving MAPK14 (p38α)-mediated pathways require further elucidation.Methods: RNA expression data and clinical information were obtained from the TCGA databases. Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis was performed using primary gastric cancer samples from GSE183904. The scRNA-seq data underwent quality control, normalization, and cell clustering in Seurat, with particular attention to SLC39A10 expression patterns in malignant epithelial cells and their association with macrophage subtypes. To validate these findings functionally, we generated stable SLC39A10 knockdown and overexpression models in human gastric cancer cell lines (HGC27 and MKN28), subsequently analyzing M2 macrophage polarization markers (CD206, Arg1, IL-10) by Western blot and to demonstrate the effects of SLC39A10 and MAPK14 on gastric cancer through in vivo and in vitro experiments.Results: Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of gastric cancer tissues identified 10 distinct cell populations, with SLC39A10 expression showing strong correlation in TAMs. GO pathway analysis revealed significant enrichment of MAPK14-related signaling pathways in Angio-TAMs. Further gene analysis of Angio-TAMs demonstrated upregulation of SLC39A10, which exhibited a strong positive correlation with MAPK14 (r=0.59). Analysis of TCGA data indicated that higher MAPK14 expression was associated with poorer overall survival in patients (p=0.018), suggesting a context-dependent role of MAPK14 in gastric cancer progression. Experimental results confirmed that both SLC39A10 and MAPK14 were highly expressed in gastric cancer cells and promoted tumor growth by facilitating M2 polarization.Conclusions:This study identifies a novel regulatory pathway mediated by SLC39A10 and MAPK14 that critically influences M2 macrophage polarization and gastric cancer progression. Targeting this signaling axis may provide a viable approach to alter the tumor microenvironment and suppress disease advancement.

title: A unique malignant cell type per patient tumor encoded in each cancer cell transcriptome
abstract: Deciphering shared features between patients through unsupervised analyses of tumor single-cell transcriptomes is hindered by the predominant clustering of malignant cells based on the patient's tumor of origin. In contrast, cancer-associated non-malignant cells within tumors cluster according to their somatic cell type (e.g. macrophage, fibroblast, astrocyte), regardless of the individual patient. We investigated the origin of this contrasting clustering behavior using computational analyses and novel data sampling techniques across 160 tumors representing 9 distinct cancer types. This led to the unexpected disclosing of tumor-specific malignant cell types. We demonstrate that tumor-driven malignant cell clustering is independent from technical or computational biases, nor is it reducible to defined gene sets with tumor-specific expression across all examined cancers. On the opposite, we unveil redundant information dispersed across the transcriptome that encodes a unique identity shared by the malignant cells within each tumor. Additionally, we found a similar genomic encoding for the identity of normal cell types. Finally, we demonstrate that malignant cell identities are maintained across space and over time, as are the identities of normal somatic cells types. These findings suggest the establishment of a distinct type of malignant cells within each tumor, robustly and diffusively encoded across the entire transcribed genome.

title: Integrating nonlinear modeling with pT stage and nodal variables: A multi-center Con-pTN model for prognosis prediction in gastric cancer (pT2–4b)
abstract: Lymph node metastasis critically determines prognosis in gastric cancer (GC), yet conventional staging inadequately captures interactions between tumor invasion depth and nodal burden. In this retrospective multi-center study, we analyzed 2,370 patients (pT2-4b) undergoing curative gastrectomy and 724 patients with SEER to develop a contour-like pTN (Con-pTN) model using a Gaussian process-augmented Cox framework that integrates pT stage, retrieved lymph nodes, and positive lymph nodes as continuous variables. Con-pTN showed robust discrimination, with area under the curves (AUCs) of 0.797 (training), 0.804 (internal validation), 0.748 (external validation cohort 1), and 0.813 (external validation cohort 2). Calibration and decision curve analyses demonstrated good agreement with observed outcomes and favorable clinical utility. Compared with pTNM, rN, and LODDS, Con-pTN provided significantly improved prognostic stratification, particularly among high-risk patients. These findings support Con-pTN as a biologically informed, clinically applicable approach for postoperative risk assessment in GC.

title: Quantitative characterization of torpor-associated behaviors in mice
abstract: Torpor is a hypometabolic and hypothermic state that enables small mammals such as mice to conserve energy under harsh conditions. While its physiological features have been extensively studied, behavioral signatures remain poorly characterized, partly due to limited quantitative tools. Here, we developed a posture-based framework to quantify torpor-associated behavior and test whether posture features help distinguish fasting-induced torpor from physiologically similar states. During torpor, mice actively suppress locomotion and adopt a curled-up posture with increased body width, head angle, and shortened body length as body temperature (Tb) falls. In contrast, adenosine monophosphate (AMP)-induced torpor-like state produces a stretched posture despite similarly reduced Tb, enabling robust discrimination. Using unsupervised analyses of aligned body-part coordinates, we further demonstrated that torpor-associated postural features differ from those during curled-up bouts in sleep and during cold exposure. These findings establish posture as a quantifiable behavioral marker that complements Tb and metabolic rate criteria and provide a noninvasive computational approach to refine torpor detection.

title: Endothelial-derived PANoptosis factor IL33 is a potential immunotherapy in breast cancer
abstract: Breast cancer (BC) heterogeneity necessitates prognostic and therapeutic biomarkers. PANoptosis remains incompletely understood with regard to its role in BC immunomodulation and clinical outcomes. Here, we integrated transcriptomic data from 7067 patients with BC across multiple cohorts. Patients were stratified via non-negative matrix factorization based on PANoptosis-related gene expression, revealing three distinct clusters. Cluster C3 exhibited the poorest overall survival, characterized by upregulated lipid metabolism and suppressed immunity. A prognostic signature was constructed using a random survival forest model and served as an independent prognostic factor. Single-cell RNA sequencing of 31 tumors identified IL-33-expressing endothelial subclusters (ACKR1 + and FBLN5 + ) as key regulators of the tumor immune microenvironment. Reduced IL-33 expression correlated with increased M2 macrophages and CD4 + T cell depletion, while sex-specific analysis revealed IL-33 as a predictor of immunotherapy response. Our findings underscore the role of PANoptosis and IL-33 + endothelial cells in shaping BC immunity and prognosis.

title: scUmaper: An automated framework for doublet removal and cell-type annotation in single-cell transcriptomics
abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing can resolve cellular heterogeneity but is sensitive to heterotypic doublets and often requires expert-driven preprocessing and annotation. We developed single cell utility matrices processing engine (scUmaper), an R/Seurat-native workflow that integrates quality control, biologically grounded doublet filtering, and marker-library-based cell-type annotation. scUmaper codifies lineage-marker incompatibility rules and applies global clustering followed by within-lineage re-clustering to reveal anomalous subclusters with implausible cross-lineage co-expression. Across six public human organ datasets, scUmaper removed additional high-confidence heterotypic doublets that were retained by simulation-based approaches and achieved annotation agreement comparable to or higher than commonly used R-based baselines, with competitive runtime. Stress tests with simulated ambient RNA contamination and reduced sequencing depth showed stable outputs under moderate degradation. scUmaper provides an interpretable and extensible framework that lowers barriers for reproducible single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis.

title: Comprehensive assessment of alternative splicing analysis methods for single-cell RNA-seq
abstract: Alternative splicing expands transcriptomic and proteomic diversity and contributes to cell identity and function. Advances in single-cell RNA sequencing enable transcriptome profiling at cellular resolution, yet their performance across biologically relevant tasks has not been systematically evaluated. Here, we benchmark six representative alternative splicing analysis methods across multiple full-length, short-read scRNA-seq datasets, focusing on biologically relevant tasks including cell clustering and differential splicing detection. Among these methods, scQuint achieves robust performance across datasets and tasks. Application of scQuint to stem cell differentiation and tumor-associated immune cell datasets identifies cell type-specific splicing programs with biological significance. These results provide guidance for method selection and highlight the value of single-cell splicing analysis for uncovering regulatory mechanisms beyond gene expression.

title: Integrating multidimensional nociceptive-related cortical features for unsupervised assessment of anesthesia states in rats
abstract: Accurate anesthesia monitoring remains challenging because current approaches primarily assess consciousness while overlooking nociceptive processing. Although electroencephalography (EEG)-based metrics such as permutation entropy (PE) and permutation cross-mutual information (PCMI) are widely used, nociceptive-evoked cortical responses, especially gamma-band oscillations (GBOs), a robust index of nociceptive intensity, are rarely incorporated into anesthesia assessment. Here, we recorded electrocorticography from 23 rats under isoflurane anesthesia with nociceptive laser stimulation during both induction and emergence. We extracted GBOs, PE, and PCMI to evaluate their sensitivity to anesthesia states. GBOs and PE tracked nociceptive-related changes during induction, whereas PCMI was more sensitive during emergence. Integrating these multidimensional features, an unsupervised k -means framework identified four latent states: awake, shallow anesthesia, moderate anesthesia, and burst suppression. These findings establish nociceptive-evoked cortical responses as label-free markers and provide a scalable foundation for real-time, closed-loop anesthesia monitoring that jointly assesses consciousness and analgesia.

title: GEP-based ecological functional zoning and land use drivers in coastal southeast China
abstract: Gross ecosystem product (GEP) assesses ecological value, but aggregate growth in urbanizing coastal zones often masks severe structural imbalances. Using the Fujian coast (2003-2023), we integrated spatiotemporal GEP accounting and spatial clustering to quantify land-use drivers and delineate functional zones. We reveal that while GEP doubled, foundational regulating services plummeted from 66.95% to 43.89%. Urban expansion triggered a "value substitution trap", where surging monetized cultural services mathematically masked the physical depletion of regulating capacities, creating a deceptive illusion of sustainability. Based on these structural shifts, five distinct ecological-economic zones were identified. These findings demonstrate that coastal governance must transcend aggregate GEP targets. Implementing spatially differentiated strategies based on internal service structures is essential to mitigate hidden ecological deficits and ensure sustainable coastal planning.

title: Molecular taxonomy and spatial organization define neuronal subtypes in the mouse inferior colliculus
abstract: The inferior colliculus (IC) is a critical auditory midbrain hub that processes sound localization and multisensory behaviors. Using single-nucleus RNA sequencing, we identify 14 transcriptionally distinct neuronal subtypes in the adult mouse IC. In situ sequencing and spatial mapping confirm these organizational patterns. Excitatory subtypes show region-specific spatial enrichment across the central, dorsal, and external cortices, whereas inhibitory subtypes are more diffusely distributed. A somatostatin-expressing ( Sst + ) neuronal population is predominantly excitatory but exhibits regional heterogeneity, with a subset co-expressing Gad2 . Sub-clustering resolves Sst + neurons into five molecularly distinct subtypes. Complementary to the Allen Brain Cell Atlas, this work provides an IC-focused molecular and spatial resource for studying neuronal diversity and cell-type-specific circuit organization in the auditory midbrain.

title: Unraveling land-use carbon-pollution co-evolution: A dynamic coordination framework with causal pathways and spatial zoning
abstract: ) pollution is increasingly used to inform differentiated regional governance, yet its temporal asynchrony, spatial clustering, and causal pathways remain insufficiently quantified. This study develops a multi-stage framework to diagnose carbon-pollution synergy across 113 district-county units in the Fenwei Plain, China, from 2013 to 2023. A process-sensitive synergistic evolution index (SEI) is constructed by integrating dynamic time warping (DTW) and a coupling coordination degree (CCD) metric to capture lag-aware co-movement and coordination. The results reveal pronounced spatial polarization in synergy performance, with significant global and local clustering patterns. Bayesian network analysis further identifies heterogeneous pathways and highlights the mediating role of urban expansion in linking ecological and anthropogenic drivers to synergy outcomes. Density-based clustering delineates four governance zones with distinct stability and enhancement potential, providing an empirical basis for spatially tailored carbon-pollution mitigation strategies.

title: Immune-associated alternative splicing signatures define molecular subtypes in breast cancer
abstract: Alternative splicing (AS) shapes tumor biology by generating mRNA isoforms that regulate oncogenic signaling, immune modulation, and therapeutic response. However, its immune-related role in breast cancer (BRCA) remains insufficiently defined. Using TCGA-BRCA RNA-seq and clinical data, we quantified percent-spliced-in values with SpliceSeq and identified 1,063 differentially expressed AS events across 861 genes. These genes were enriched in cancer- and immune-related pathways, including focal adhesion, VEGF signaling, and cytokine-receptor interactions. Prognostic analyses revealed immune-associated AS events linked to overall survival and progression-free interval. Consensus clustering defined three AS-based subtypes with distinct immune landscapes and outcomes. C3 showed high immune infiltration, immune-activating molecule expression, and favorable prognosis, consistent with an immune-hot phenotype, whereas C1 displayed immunosuppressive features. Genomic alterations in splicing factors were associated with elevated tumor mutation burden, suggesting genomic instability may contribute to immune-related splicing dysregulation in BRCA.
